legalCaveat: The 2020 decree is an additional source-bound traditional rubric; applicable later law/local permissions and exact formulary must be independently established. No software decision can substitute for a competent celebrant/ordinary.

outputSurfaces.calendar: Explain why an observance is displayed, omitted, transferred, only potentially eligible, or locally scoped.
outputSurfaces.mass: Only a positively sourced and independently checked local selection may change the Mass; unreviewed advisory alternatives never enter the reader or ICS.

rules.outcome: The observed 1962 principal observance and commemoration schedule remain the default. No modern sainthood record replaces the day main or its Mass Proper.
Decide precedence, omission, commemoration, first-class accidental transfer and permanent reassignment by actual source/rubrics; a weekday feast does not automatically transfer to Sunday.
Distinguish privileged from ordinary commemorations; St Peter and St Paul have an inseparable commemoration under one conclusion.
Only privileged commemorations are admitted; the number, precedence and any further restrictions must be resolved with the full Mass rubrics.
Only one commemoration, of a second-class feast, unless a privileged commemoration must instead be made. Ordinary weekday saints are not eligible merely because their feast fell that week.
Only one commemoration, privileged or ordinary, subject to precedence and exclusions.
At most two commemorations, subject to exclusions, priority and any sung Mass restrictions.
Prevent prayers to the same saint twice or incompatible mysteries; season comes first, then order of precedence; omit excess under the actual cap.

After effective date 2020-03-19 and only on an independently established universal-church liturgical memorial date, consider a festive Mass on permitted III-class days or III-class saint vigils (and applicable IV-class provisions); require just cause and no contrary rubrical obstacle.
The 70 named III-class feasts cannot be impeded by the decree; compare exact canonical source identities, not titles or date alone.
Commemorate the omitted traditional feast/vigil and other required observances within applicable numerical and ritual rules.
Choose 1962 Proprium pro aliquibus locis first, then approved Holy See Supplement, then 1962 Common. Never import the postconciliar lectionary/formulary.
Optional commemoration is limited to a saint or mystery on the date listed in approved Proprium pro aliquibus locis or Supplement; modern calendar mention alone is insufficient.
The house superior, not an individual celebrant, decides the application of these options in common celebrations.
Include documented titular, dedication, patronal, order and local observances only for the applicable location/community; preserve 1962 precedence and valid indults.

A permitted external solemnity is a specific votive Mass of the feast, without changing the Office, governed by entitlement by law or indult, day restrictions and the prescribed Mass count; not a blanket weekday commemoration.
A later Doctor proclamation updates one existing person profile as of its declaration date; does not create a second person or second feast.
Show historic principal, actual 1962 commemorations, eligible alternatives, supplementary saints and devotional observances under distinct labels without duplicate canonical identities.
